landmark_cases.title: Campbell v. Acuff-Rose Music, Inc.
landmark_cases.reason: Canonical fair use decision clarifying the four-factor analysis, emphasizing transformative purpose, parody, and that market harm asks whether the secondary work is a substitute rather than merely critical.

landmark_cases.title: Hachette Book Group, Inc. v. Internet Archive
landmark_cases.reason: Recent controlling Second Circuit articulation of fair use, especially factor four’s focus on usurpation of markets versus harm from criticism, and the flexible, context-specific nature of fair use.

landmark_cases.title: Authors Guild v. Google, Inc.
landmark_cases.reason: Seminal Second Circuit precedent on transformative use and socially beneficial secondary purposes (search, commentary), informing factor one analysis.

landmark_cases.title: Cariou v. Prince
landmark_cases.reason: Key Second Circuit case on transformative appropriation and that courts may assess fair use by examining the works themselves, supporting resolution without extensive discovery.

landmark_cases.title: TCA Television Corp. v. McCollum
landmark_cases.reason: Establishes that fair use can be resolved at the Rule 12(b)(6) stage when clear from the complaint and incorporated materials.

landmark_cases.title: Lama Holding Co. v. Smith Barney Inc.
landmark_cases.reason: Foundational New York Court of Appeals decision on fraudulent inducement damages, requiring out-of-pocket loss—central to the state-law dismissal.
